html:
The Rajatarangini, "River of Kings", is a verse history of the kings of Kashmir written in Sanskrit by the poet Kalhana in 1148 and 1149.

It has eight books and about 7,800 verses. It runs from legendary beginnings to Kalhana's own day. The early parts mix myth with fact, but the later books, close to his own time, are detailed and often critical of the kings they describe.

What makes it stand out is method. Kalhana says he read older chronicles, land grants and temple inscriptions, and he tried to weigh them. For this it is often called the first real work of history in Sanskrit. A century earlier al-Biruni had complained that Indians paid little attention to the order of events; Kalhana is the great exception.

It is the main source for Kashmir kings such as Lalitaditya. Later writers carried the story on into the time of the sultans, and modern historians still use it, with care.
sum: The Rajatarangini, "River of Kings", is a verse history of the kings of Kashmir written in Sanskrit by the poet Kalhana in 1148 and 1149.
